messages:
sophie: FYI Havenly submitted a POC request. Target: sustained 120 qps per region, avg request ~256 tokens, p99 < 300ms, multi-region active/passive with failover. They prefer Private but are open to Dedicated. Also attached a security questionnaire asking about KMS and key rotation. Need runbook + quick pricing delta hosted vs dedicated. Can we do next-week run? cc @raj @jules

raj: Sounds doable. Need model variant and whether they accept batching + KV prefix cache. Batching changes throughput curve a lot for long contexts.

sophie: They asked for a privacy-minded quant model: "redwood-ggml-large-q4". Batching ok but want to preserve <300ms p99. They're worried KMS will decrypt on every call (envelope keys).

jules: Draft run plan:
1) warmup: 15m at 20 qps to populate KV cache
2) ramp: 20 -> 120 qps over 25m
3) soak: 4h at 120 qps collect p50/p90/p95/p99 + per-token cost
4) spike test: 30m at 240 qps to validate autoscale/fallback
5) failover: simulate us-west1 -> eu-west1 switch and validate tail latencies
Include traces at 1% and request sampling for detailed spans.

matt: Ops notes:
- set request timeout 6s, per-worker concurrency cap 10
- enable KV prefix caching and pre-warm prompts library
- provision a small fallback model (fp16) with automatic reroute policy
- capture cold-starts and KMS request latencies separately
I'll run this on 2026-04-07 08:00 PT unless you want sooner.

raj: Performance caveats: q4 quant is memory-efficient but can show higher variability with long sequences. Recommend we run both q4 and fp16 for head-to-head comparison. Dedicated sizing estimate: 6x A100-equivalent GPUs gives safe headroom for 120 qps with our batching profile.

finance-bot: Preliminary cost stub (rough): Hosted (q4): ~$600/day for 4h soak + supporting traffic and infra. Dedicated (pro-rated test): ~$210/day equivalent (assuming shared reserved pool) + KMS request charges and egress. Finalize after exact GPU-hours and KMS count.

security-bot: New questionnaire created: https://redwood-internal/q/HVN-2026-KMS. Key points to answer: envelope key flow, whether KMS decrypts per request, DEK caching TTL, HSM-backed KMS options, and audit log availability.

sophie: Important: Havenly requires confirmation that KMS won't be called per-response in Private/Dedicated. Can someone write a short explainer and sequence diagram for the questionnaire.

jules: Short explainer: in Private/Dedicated we use envelope encryption. KMS unwrap is performed at DEK generation or rotation, DEK cached in the runtime with TTL and KMS calls are not made per inference request. Will produce a one-pager and a diagram for the security response.

matt: I'll add a quick handshake smoke that rotates keys and measures the latency impact, plus a trace label for KMS-unwrap spans. Also will surface HSM latency if they pick HSM-backed KMS.

raj: Load test snippet (fortio example):
```
# fortio single duration, 120 rps, 4h, json output
fortio load -qps 120 -t 4h -c 120 -payload ./payload.json https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate > fortio-hvn-120rps.json
# payload.json uses prompt_len ~256 and batching disabled/enabled variants
```
Capture per-request headers: model, seq_len, cache-hit, kms-span-id.

sophie: Can we have final runbook + cost stub + the KMS explainer by EOD today? Havenly wants something to review before sign-off.

jules: I'll assemble runbook + one-pager KMS explainer and post by 17:00 PT. Raj will post GPU sizing and perf caveats. Matt will schedule the run and include the smoke scripts.

matt: Scheduled: tentative run 2026-04-07T15:00:00Z, run id: hvn-poc-2026-04-07. I'll tag ops channel and supply access for Havenly to view sanitized traces.

finance-bot: Note: if they require HSM-backed KMS and Private deployment, add ~15-25% to dedicated cost for HSM-provisioning and audit retention.

sophie: Thanks all. If you can attach the runbook and the quick pricing table here when ready I will send to the customer.
